messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "The air feels different lately — not like change is here, but like it’s getting ready to land. Just keeping my head down and watching the quiet ones, because the ones who’ve stopped speaking are usually the ones who’ve made up their minds."
Sender 2: "The pharmacist just told me he’s hoarding meds — not for sale, for his family. Word is spreading quietly, even the usual chatter on the square feels different. Be careful what you say, and keep your phone charged."
Sender 3: "The quiet seems heavier than before — things are running smoother than they have in years, and people are starting to breathe again. Still, the fact that even the smallest details are being handled with precision makes me wonder if this calm is the eye of the storm, not the end of it."
Sender 4: "The quiet is louder than noise these days — things are holding together on the surface, but something’s off. I’ve heard from family in the provinces, and life there feels normal, which makes me think the real trouble is behind closed doors."
Sender 5: "The air’s different lately—people are talking again, even if quietly. I’ve heard whispers about the capital’s flights filling up and the usual silence in the streets starting to crack. Let’s stay sharp, keep our heads down, and watch the quiet signs."
Sender 6: "The weather’s been so strange lately—sun one day, storm the next. I’ve been packing an extra sweater just in case. You know how it is."
Sender 7: "The weather’s been strange this week — early frost, then sudden warmth. I’ve been meaning to ask if you’ve noticed how people are talking more freely, even in the market. Seems like everyone’s waiting to see what happens when the city lights go out again."
Sender 8: "It’s quiet here, but the kind of quiet that feels like holding your breath — like something’s about to shift, though nobody’s sure what or how. Just keep your eyes open, and for now, keep talking in code."
Sender 9: "Just wanted to say — the tea house crowd’s been talking a lot lately, and not just about the weather. It’s getting harder to ignore how things are shifting, even if no one’s saying it outright. Keep the lines open, watch the quiet ones, and don’t leave anything behind."
Sender 10: "The streets feel different — quieter, but with a kind of held breath. I’ve been told to keep my windows closed this week, just in case."

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 10 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 10.
